lead: Alphabet / GOOGL — the split that lets small accounts in
smaller: PayPal / PYPL — the fintech dip gets a trapdoor
Exxon Mobil / XOM — Big Oil pays you to wait
Solana / SOL — the NFT chain gets its festival moment
why_lead: Alphabet's 20-for-1 split announced with its 1 February results (CNBC n0806, Shacknews n0805) is the clearest new crowd catalyst of the day: a mega-cap with a four-figure share price (GOOGL 2,752.88 USD, +1.73% 1-session, +8.44% 5-session, -5.07% 20-session) becoming accessible, backed by record results and an after-hours pop (Reuters n0095, The Verge n1119, Seattle Times n1108, Deadline n0870). Attention evidence is coverage breadth plus live options appetite elsewhere (AMC call-buying surge n0820; Yahoo stock-splits calendar n0097); smart-money split is Morgan Stanley's Sheets (n0390) and its Apple top pick (n0647) vs Standard Chartered's flattening/inversion call (n2045). Relation to the only strictly earlier retail note (2022-02-01: GameStop lead; Netflix, Spotify, ARKK smaller): no ticker or narrative repeats; the meme proxies (GME, HOOD) appear only as supporting attention data, not as a recycled lead.
why_smaller: PayPal / PYPL: a distinct broken-dip narrative — the stock had rebounded 11.13% over five sessions to 175.80 USD, Wolfe Research's Darrin Peller was bullish on CNBC (n0866), then CNBC reported it plunging on weak guidance (n0831); the sympathy risk to Block (+10.68% 5-session), Affirm (+23.77%) and Upstart (+24.55%) and the IRS $600 reporting headline (n1135) define where it breaks.

Exxon Mobil / XOM: a distinct energy-windfall narrative — biggest profit in seven years (n0788), $8.9 billion quarter (n0786), $23 billion 2021 and a $10 billion buyback (n1268), XOM +6.41% to 80.83 USD and +27.21% over 20 sessions with WTI 88.20 USD/bbl; breaks on OPEC supply (n1844), Deutsche Bank's energy-price question (n1226) and Permian supply growth (n1116).

Solana / SOL: a distinct altcoin-comeback narrative — Coachella's Solana NFTs with FTX (n0952), Phantom's $109 million raise (n0946), FTX's $32 billion valuation (n0667); SOL +10.27% to 109.98 USD and +22.70% over five days vs bitcoin +4.32%; breaks on NFT scepticism (n0958), DeFi exploits (Qubit n0916) and India's 30% tax (n0956).
considered_not_chosen: Digital World Acquisition / DWAC (+13.93% 1-session, +20.69% 5-session, +61.03% 20-session): biggest equity move on the card but no own-date headline explaining it, so not written.

AMD (+10% after hours on a strong 2022 outlook, n0744): a beat-and-raise chip story better suited to sector coverage; the day's distinct crowd narratives were the split, the broken fintech dip, oil and Solana.
AMC call-buying surge (n0820): used as options-attention evidence in the lead rather than as a separate meme item, to avoid recycling the 2022-02-01 GameStop lead without a material change.
AT&T dividend cut of 47% (n0747, T -4.24%): an income-investor story without broad retail-attention evidence.
Netflix (+24.76% 5-session) and Spotify (+10.64% 5-session): both were 2022-02-01 smaller items with no materially new own-date evidence; Spotify's results are pending after the cutoff.
Meta Platforms (FB) results pending on 2 February after the cutoff with no own-date dated preview; not used.

Not used: n0720 (CNBC 'Stocks rise for a third day ... Dow jumps 270 points', stamped 2022-01-31 but apparently describing the 1 February session, i.e. a misdated stamp); not needed.
